title: Fish Tacos
subtitle: Beer-battered cod, crunchy slaw, chipotle mayo
excerpt: Light, crispy beer-battered cod tucked into warm corn tortillas with crunchy cabbage slaw and a smoky chipotle mayonnaise. A coastal Tex-Mex classic that comes together in under 30 minutes.
sourceNotes: Beer-battered fish tacos: a Baja California-influenced Tex-Mex dish that became a US restaurant and home staple. Classic form documented in Tex-Mex home-cooking sources and coastal American cooking traditions.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The slaw and chipotle mayo can both be made up to a day ahead and refrigerated.

glossaryTerms.definition: A thin mixture of flour, liquid, and sometimes egg used to coat food before frying, producing a crisp golden crust.

content.text: Fish tacos are warm corn tortillas filled with crispy beer-

cod, a sharp cabbage slaw, and a smoky chipotle mayo. The batter is light and barely seasoned so the fish comes through. Oil temperature is the key: 180°C gives a pale, greasy crust; 190-200°C gives a crisp one that holds.

items.prepNote: dried chipotle, finely chopped, or 1 tsp chipotle paste

content.text: Use a deep, wide frying pan rather than a shallow one for frying; the fish needs to float freely. A probe thermometer takes the guesswork out of the oil temperature.
Make the slaw and chipotle mayo
Toss the shredded cabbage with the coriander and the juice of 1 lime. Season with salt. Set aside.
Stir the finely chopped chipotle and lime juice into the mayonnaise. Taste and add more chipotle if you want more heat. Refrigerate until needed.
Make the batter and fry the fish

Whisk {{plain-flour}} of flour with {{cayenne}} of cayenne and a pinch of salt. Pour in {{beer}} of cold beer and whisk to a smooth batter roughly the consistency of single cream. Don't overwork it; a few lumps are fine.

Heat {{vegetable-oil}} of oil in a deep frying pan to 190-200°C. Pat the cod strips dry with kitchen paper; wet fish steams rather than fries. Dip each strip in the batter, let the excess drip off, and lower carefully into the oil.
Fry in batches for 3-4 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. Drain on kitchen paper. Season with salt immediately.
Warm each tortilla in a dry pan for 30 seconds a side. Stack and cover. Set out the slaw, chipotle mayo, jalapeño, and lime wedges. Fill the tortillas: slaw first, fish on top, mayo drizzled over.

items.cause: Fish not dried properly, or oil too cool
items.fix: Pat fish very dry before battering. Wet fish creates steam that lifts the batter off. Check oil temperature before each batch.
The oil must reach 190-200°C. Adding too much fish at once drops the temperature sharply; fry in small batches.

items.cause: Too much flour or batter mixed in advance
items.fix: Make the batter just before frying. Add more cold beer to thin it to a single-cream consistency.
Warm each one in a dry pan until flexible. Wrap in a tea towel to keep them pliable.

content.text: Fish tacos have roots in the coastal cooking of Baja California, where fried or grilled fish in tortillas has been a street-food staple for generations. The beer-battered version crossed the border into the US Southwest and became a Tex-Mex restaurant fixture by the late twentieth century. The combination of hot crunchy fish, cold crisp slaw, and smoky mayo in a warm tortilla is a study in contrast that's hard to beat.
